nativeMessaging: Talks to the local companion program that the user's coding agent starts, so routines and recorded runs reach the agent and the agent can drive the browser. Nothing is sent over the network by this.
tabs: Opens, switches and reads the address and title of tabs, so a routine can run in the tab it was started for and the panel can show which site it is on.
scripting: Injects the content script into pages that were open before the extension loaded, so recording and replay work without a reload.
storage: Keeps settings, the list of recent runs and the signed-in session on this device.
identity: Runs the Google sign-in window. Sign-in is optional and is only used to tie routines to an account.
sidePanel: Shows the Agentic Routines panel: the saved routines, what the agent has recorded, and the replay controls where the person approves a paused step.
tabGroups: Puts the tab an agent is working in into a group named for that agent, so the person can see which tabs are in use and by whom. The tab leaves the group when the agent is done. Tabs already in one of the person's own groups are left alone.
debugger: Used for four things a normal extension cannot do: set a local file on a page's file input (uploads), take a screenshot of a tab that is behind another or a window on a hidden desktop, click and type in a tab that is not in front without switching the person to it, and draw one frame in a window that has stopped drawing. It is attached for the length of one action and detached straight after.
<all_urls>: The user's coding agent works on whichever sites the user asks it to, and routines are replayed on those sites, so the extension cannot list them ahead of time. It acts only on the tab the agent is working in.
